clue.text: Thought men carrying gift around funny

indicators.note: around says the scrambled gift goes on either side of the word men
funny means odd or peculiar, so the letters of gift are made strange and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some men are carrying a present that looks rather odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'men carrying' tempts you to put men on the outside, but 'around' sends the jumbled gift (FIGT, from 'funny') round them; 'carrying' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is something merely imagined, an invented notion of the mind.

clue.text: Large Persians are important people

explanation.surface: Big pedigree cats are the VIPs.
explanation.definitionFit: Overweight felines are literally plump moggies; the phrase is also slang for wealthy, powerful bigwigs.

clue.text: Polish chap found in Venice?

parts.note: it looks like a man from Poland on holiday, but the man is a Venetian boatman who poles his craft along the canals

explanation.surface: A Polish man spotted in Venice.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Polish' as 'pole-ish': one who propels a boat with a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: Venetian canal boats are propelled by a standing oarsman with a long pole or oar.

clue.text: Inspiration for some writer at ode

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A source of inspiration for some poet at work on an ode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' only links. The run comes from writ(ER AT O)de.
explanation.definitionFit: Erato is the Muse of lyric and love poetry, a goddess who inspires poets.

clue.text: He's green about gold

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the heraldic green is reversed

parts.note: vert is the heraldic word for green
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A man described as an environmentalist concerned with gold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' defines a man's name. Both colours are heraldic terms: VERT green, OR gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Trevor is a common male first name, so it can stand for a man.

clue.text: A horse and farm animal is a mix of characters

parts.note: a nag is an old or worn-out horse
a ram is a male sheep kept on a farm

explanation.surface: A horse and a sheep together make a curious jumble of letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This kind of word puzzle is literally a rearrangement of the letters of a word or phrase.

clue.text: In the open man forces change

parts.note: Al is a short man's name

indicators.note: change tells you to alter the order of the letters of forces

explanation.surface: Out in the open air, a man compels a transformation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' for a short name like AL is a crossword habit; 'change' gives FRESCO from the clue's forces, and the surface's 'In the open' is the whole definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Done outdoors, as in an open-air meal, is the Italian-derived phrase meaning 'in the cool'.

clue.text: George requiring no help when stacking?

definitions.text: George requiring no help when stacking?

parts.words: George requiring no help when stacking?
parts.note: George is old pilots' slang for the device that flies a plane; stacking is aircraft circling in a holding pattern

explanation.surface: Someone named George manages to pile things up without assistance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stacking' suggests piling things up, but it means aircraft circling at staggered heights waiting to land.
explanation.definitionFit: The automatic flight-control system steers the aircraft without the pilot's hands on the controls.

clue.text: German assent after Brazilian port and Spanish wine

indicators.note: after puts the German word second, following the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a major Brazilian port
ja is German for yes

explanation.surface: A German says yes after reaching a South American harbour and a Spanish wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Rioja is a red wine from the region of northern Spain of that name.

clue.text: Contrary girl set out to be in full command

indicators.note: to be in places the scrambled letters inside the girl's name

parts.note: from the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary'

indicators.note: out means disordered, so the letters of set are rearranged

explanation.surface: A stubborn girl sets out to take total charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary girl' points to the nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary'; 'out' jumbles set to STE and 'to be in' lodges it inside her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Mastery is complete control or expert skill over something.

clue.text: Ship's capacity Anne got wrong

indicators.note: something got wrong is muddled up, so the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: Anne miscalculated how much cargo a ship can carry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got wrong' rearranges the seven letters of ANNE GOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonnage is the measured cargo volume or carrying weight of a vessel.

clue.text: Comes to understand units of measurement

explanation.surface: Someone finally grasps how lengths are measured.
explanation.definitionFit: To fathom is to get to the bottom of, i.e. grasp; a fathom is also a six-foot unit of depth used at sea.

clue.text: A glutton will have this — busy people too

explanation.surface: Both greedy eaters and overworked people have something in common.
explanation.definitionFit: A greedy eater literally piles food high on the dish; the idiom also means having too much work to cope with.

clue.text: Change over electrical apparatus

explanation.surface: Replacing a piece of electrical gear.
explanation.definitionFit: To swap one thing for another is to make a swap or exchange; a device for turning a circuit on or off is also so called.

clue.text: Slogan makes crowd chat in an excited manner

indicators.note: in an excited manner suggests agitated jumbling, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A rallying cry gets a crowd talking excitedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' only links; the nine letters of CROWD CHAT are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A catchword is a popular phrase or motto taken up by a group.

clue.text: Room for the oarsman at front of yacht

parts.note: a sculler is a rower who uses a pair of sculls

indicators.note: at front of picks out only the opening letter of the word yacht

explanation.surface: Space set aside for a rower at the bow of a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: A SCULLERY is a back kitchen for washing up in a traditional British house; 'for the' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A scullery is a small back kitchen in a house, used for washing dishes.

clue.text: Try an overdue criminal

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Put on trial a crook who is overdue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges AN OVERDUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an attempt or effort, as in 'make every endeavour'.

clue.text: Surface designer sobers me up

indicators.note: up here means in disorder or amiss, as in 'what's up', so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A designer of finishes sobers me up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' looks like part of 'sobers up' but signals rearranging SOBERS ME.
explanation.definitionFit: An embosser stamps raised patterns onto paper, metal or leather, decorating the outer layer.

clue.text: Damage one enemy of the sea

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
the Roman numeral for one is I
time is often called the enemy, as in the saying 'time is the enemy'

explanation.surface: Harming a foe of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: TIME for 'enemy' comes from the phrase 'time is the enemy', a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime describes anything relating to the ocean or to seafaring.

clue.text: Interpret loudly and run away

parts.note: to make of something is to interpret it, as in 'what do you make of this?'
f stands for forte, the musical direction to play loudly

explanation.surface: Read something out at volume and then flee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loudly' is F (forte) in music, not a sign that words are spoken.
explanation.definitionFit: To make off is to leave hurriedly, to flee.

clue.text: Going west, say, spots treacle pudding?

indicators.note: in an across clue going west means read from right to left, so the joined pieces are turned round

parts.note: say means for example, abbreviated eg
spots are dots

explanation.surface: A spotted pudding heading off westward, as it were.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going west' turns the whole run EGDOTS. The question mark marks treacle pudding as just one example of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling food, and a steamed sweet sponge is a classic case.

clue.text: Increase points to Chinese folk at church

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
the Han are China's majority ethnic group
CE is short for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Compass points lead to Chinese people at a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'at' only link the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To enhance is to improve or boost something, making it greater.

clue.text: Daft bears I had

parts.note: bears means puts up with, and puts written upwards in a down clue reads stup
I'd is a contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Teddy bears I owned were silly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bears' is PUTS UP, read literally in a down entry: PUTS going up gives STUP.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupid means foolish or lacking good sense.

clue.text: It's an honour to have time in the evening to wash, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells you the phrase is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.words: time in the evening to wash
parts.note: night is a time in the evening, and the bath is the time to wash: night of the bath

explanation.surface: It is a privilege to get an evening soak.
explanation.walkthrough: This British order of chivalry sounds like a night spent bathing; 'to have' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: The Order of the Bath is a British order of chivalry, and membership of it is a royal award.

clue.text: Foolish son deserts bats

indicators.note: deserts means leaves, so the letter for son is taken out

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy, mad

explanation.surface: A boy runs away from flying bats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' is the adjective meaning mad, not the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly, senseless or empty-headed.

clue.text: Makes ready for work?

parts.note: it reads like preparing for a job, but ready is slang for cash, so it means gaining money for labour

explanation.surface: Preparing someone for a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is slang for money, as in 'ready cash'; making money for working is the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To be paid for one's labour is to receive wages for it.

clue.text: Cicero and Churchill were painters — but not last month

indicators.note: but not tells you to remove the following piece from the word before

parts.note: painters and decorators do up houses, so painters are decorators
the last month of the year is December, abbreviated DEC

explanation.surface: A claim that two famous statesmen once worked as painters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'were' is a link; Churchill did paint, which makes the false trail more tempting.
explanation.definitionFit: Both were celebrated public speakers famed for their rhetoric.

clue.text: Eddy has nothing in lift

parts.note: purl is a swirling eddy or ripple in a stream
the letter O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A man called Eddy has no money in an elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: Lift here is slang for steal, and purloin likewise means to take dishonestly.

clue.text: A slip, perhaps, if backing into tree

indicators.note: backing means moving backwards, so the word if is read in reverse

parts.note: the little word if is used as written before being turned round
the elder is a small tree with dark berries

explanation.surface: A small error, should someone reverse into a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns IF into FI, which runs into ELDER. SLIP is a cricket fielding position near the batsman, so a slip is one kind of fielder.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a player stationed at slip is one of the team's catchers in the field.

clue.text: Earn notes to play some tennis

parts.note: D and E are musical notes
to serve is to put the ball into play in tennis

explanation.surface: Musicians earn their keep by playing tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: To merit something, to have it coming, is to be worthy of it.
